original_operations.name: TID cached once in actual thread_local
TimeTicks native platform selection and conversion

selections: CurrentProcessId and CurrentThreadId project actual native identifiers with the original int conversion; CurrentThreadId alone caches its original platform observation in static thread_local int.
Native Windows/Linux/Android/Darwin are the intended source selections. Other V8-specific AIX/Fuchsia/Solaris/Starboard branches are not claimed by this component.

Trace-consumed TimeTicks::Now and ThreadTicks::Now return their signed microsecond internal value directly. FromMicroseconds(x) and ToInternalValue are representation wrappers; the original zero TimeTicks plus TimeDelta saturating addition is exactly x for every already represented int64.

Windows QPC initialization probes performance frequency and the real invariant-TSC predicate in the original order. Low-resolution fallback preserves the original last-top-byte/16-bit-rollover state and atomic CAS publication.
The exact original time.h QPC boundary literal 0x8637BD05AF7 is retained, including the strict-less-than branch. No floor-threshold approximation remains.

The invariant-TSC field is specialized from CPU(): original leaf0 and leaf1 hypervisor gate, extended-leaf bound, invariant bit and exact Microsoft Hyper-V exception. Unused CPU fields and their unrelated feature probes are absent. Original Windows ARM64 field is true.

Windows x86/x64 CPU ticks use actual QueryThreadCycleTime divided by the independently measured RDTSC frequency, not QueryPerformanceFrequency. Initial evaluation under50ms returns zero. Raising/restoring current thread priority, initial readings and later calibration order are retained.
Windows ARM64 preserves the original user FILETIME-only CPU observation; memcpy reproduces the original bit_cast representation operation before dividing100ns units by10.

Darwin retains original mach_timebase_info initialization/division order and sums actual thread_info user+system microseconds. Linux/Android retain real clock_gettime, the original upper-second check and wall-clock plus1.

Release DCHECK expressions remain unevaluated; no IsSupported or waiting call was added to the controller CPU-sampling path. The caller must guard explicit WaitForCpuTimestampInitializationNative with CpuTimestampSupportedNative, matching ThreadTicks public contract.
review_notes: No source generator, compiler, AST, formatter, Node, target or runtime process was executed. Static Python work only copied known immutable originals, verified hashes and recorded this packet.

Actual Abseil V8Mutex and platform Recorder admission, native trace API and startup composition remain separate required owners.
Native clock/worker/concurrent observations and negative clock diagnostics require separate meaningful controls, build/link and Root-owned runtime validation.

The original Windows timestamp function-pointer/frequency and TSC-frequency publication protocol is retained, including its source concurrency assumptions; no stronger thread-race qualification is claimed.
No whole-process/foreground clock, cross-platform, controller or application qualification is established.
